text:
Hidden Word · 5–6 players · 2 rounds

Each player privately chooses one envelope containing five common nouns.
In the drawn order, each player becomes the setter once per round. In the first round, choose one of the words you received;
In Round 2, choose the hidden word from the four words not used in Round 1.
As the setter, earn points while concealing your answer. As a guesser, identify the other players’ words to pursue survival and victory.

Every hint candidate submitted by the setter and its normalized score are immediately revealed to all players.
Across all three phases for the same hidden word, previously public hint candidates or final clues cannot be submitted again.
Each hint phase allows at most fifteen minutes and ten hints.
When a normalized score exceeds 95 points, hint submission ends immediately and that word is highlighted as the final clue.
If the threshold has not been exceeded by the time ten hints have been submitted or time runs out,
If no hint exceeds the threshold, reveal the closest noun from the full Standard Korean Language Dictionary, excluding the answer and all words already made public.
If the highest similarity is tied, choose the word that appears first in the dictionary.
All candidate words, scores and final clues from earlier phases remain visible in later phases.

Everyone except the setter submits their guesses simultaneously and privately within five minutes.
Once per hidden word, you may spend one Piece to submit one additional answer. The Piece is spent regardless of whether the answer is correct.
Each correct guesser earns one VP, and that setter's turn ends.
If nobody guesses correctly, the setter earns one point in phase 1, two in phase 2 and three in phase 3.
Hint submission and guessing repeat up to three times, and the setter's points from unsuccessful guessing phases accumulate.
All VP awards are doubled in Round 2. Reveal the hidden word when the final phase ends or someone guesses correctly.

After round 2, three players enter the Prison Wing and the lowest-ranked player is eliminated. The remaining top players enter the Living Quarters: one in a five-player match or two in a six-player match.
First place receives four Pieces. This match has no Alliance Token reprieve.

Simulation procedure
The simulator uses original common-noun envelopes rather than the broadcast’s envelopes. Nearest-word reveals and normalization use the June 5, 2026 dictionary snapshot.
The game uses 213,810 nouns from the Standard Korean Language Dictionary and Cohere embed-v5.0-pro embeddings.
Submitted hints are scored through embeddings whether or not they appear in the dictionary.
Each hint must be one noun or nominal term written entirely in Hangul, without Latin letters, digits or symbols.
Submit a single noun or term. On its first submission, a hint absent from the dictionary is embedded using the same Cohere model and cached.
This cache is used only to score hints. Automatic nearest-word clues and the 99.9-point normalization reference are determined solely from the fixed dictionary of 213,810 nouns.
All players use the same model and reference dictionary, with cosine similarity calculated locally.
Scores are normalized with the nearest dictionary noun other than the answer set to 99.9 points.
Divide cosine similarity by the cosine similarity of the nearest dictionary noun, multiply by 100, and limit the result to 0–99.9 points.
These normalization and reveal criteria are simulator rules.
The scores are not guaranteed to match those of the model trained for the broadcast. Players' providers, models and call limits do not affect similarity.
Words and scores for out-of-dictionary hints are also immediately public. Embedding request errors stop the match rather than count as invalid hints.
Scripted actions use the same embedding-based scoring.
In the simulator, the answer itself cannot be submitted as a hint.
The broadcast uses six players. A campaign with five survivors from the previous match proceeds with five, without adding a returning player.
Players privately summarize their strategies before the game and before submitting guesses.
For each hint, privately plan, draft and review before submitting the final hint and a short decision summary.
Each of the four stages uses a separate model call. Drafts are neither scored nor shown to other players.
There is no player discussion, negotiation, whispering or room movement.
This match does not update affinity or trust assessments.
The hint timer includes planning, drafting, review and final submission. Answer submission combines each guesser's strategy summary and answer response time.
Waiting time is not simulated separately.
Complete ties are resolved by the drawn order announced at the start. Invalid formats or actions after the call limit use scripted demonstration actions.
